criteria.criterion: producer_brief in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs emits a section, placed before the Checks section, that tells the producer not to write the boundary-scan words and fragments (singular, plural and hyphenated forms included) in any file, and explains that the scan is whole-word and case-insensitive.
criteria.evidence: Read in the diff: producer_brief writes banned_words_section() right before "## Checks Athena will run". The section is titled "Words you must not write". It lists all 17 words, including the plural and hyphenated forms, and the 6 fragments. It says "Do not write these words in any file you touch" and that "The scan matches whole words, case-insensitively". I checked that wording against boundary_scan in xtask/tests/policy.rs: it matches words with (?i)\b...\b and fragments as lowercase substrings, so the claim is accurate.

criteria.criterion: No tracked file contains a banned term literally. The Rust source builds each term from fragments, as xtask/tests/policy.rs does, and crates/athena-context/prompts/producer.md stays free of them.
criteria.evidence: Read in the diff: briefs.rs builds every term from two-part arrays joined with concat(). The new line in producer.md names only the section and the scan, not the words. The boundary-scan test athena_refers_to_no_one_who_runs_it_or_where passed when I ran it on this tree.

criteria.criterion: A new unit test in athena-context renders a producer brief and asserts it names every word in the boundary list. Run `cargo test -p athena-context`.
criteria.evidence: The new test producer_briefs_list_the_boundary_words_before_the_checks renders a brief and asserts it contains every word and fragment, the whole-word wording, and that the section comes before the checks. Without the change the test would fail. I ran the athena-context tests: 17 passed, including this one.

criteria.criterion: The full suite passes, including athena_refers_to_no_one_who_runs_it_or_where, and clippy is clean. Run `cargo test --locked` and `cargo clippy --all-targets`.
criteria.evidence: I ran the full suite with cargo test --locked: every test binary reported ok, with 0 failures. The policy suite, which includes athena_refers_to_no_one_who_runs_it_or_where, had 9 of 9 pass. cargo clippy --all-targets printed nothing.

criteria.criterion: The word list has one stated owner, or a test fails when the brief's list and the xtask scanner's list differ. The list cannot drift silently.
criteria.evidence: The new xtask test the_producer_brief_lists_exactly_the_scanners_terms checks that athena_context::briefs::boundary_words and boundary_fragments equal the scanner's own lists, so the lists cannot drift without a test failing. athena-context is added to xtask as a dev-dependency only, and dependency_direction_matches_the_architecture still passes.

criteria.criterion: The M19 row in docs/enforcement.md mentions that the producer brief lists the banned words up front. The row stays accurate and still passes the enforcement-map test.
criteria.evidence: Read in the diff: the M19 mechanism cell now says the producer brief lists the banned words up front and names the parity test. every_test_named_in_the_enforcement_map_exists passed.

findings.summary: The word list exists in two copies, in athena-context and in the xtask scanner, rather than one shared owner. A test ties the copies together.
findings.evidence: This is allowed by criterion 5 and recorded as a tradeoff in D73. Making the scanner read the brief's list would remove the duplicate.

summary: The change does what was asked. The producer brief now has a "Words you must not write" section, placed before the checks. It lists every word and fragment the boundary scan rejects, including the plural and hyphenated forms, and it says the scan matches whole words, case-insensitively. I checked that against the scanner's code and it is accurate. The terms are built from fragments, so no tracked file contains them, and the boundary scan still passes. A unit test checks that the brief names every term and that the section comes before the checks. A second test, in xtask, fails if the brief's list and the scanner's list ever differ; it relies on a dev-only dependency, which leaves the documented dependency graph unchanged. The M19 row in docs/enforcement.md, the D73 entry in docs/decisions.md and the changelog are updated. I ran the athena-context tests, the policy tests, the full suite and clippy myself: all pass, and clippy reported nothing.
